stories.headline: HBCU on-campus shooting leaves one dead, three shot following homecoming
stories.summary: Two separate shootings on the Winston-Salem State University campus on Saturday night, during the HBCU's homecoming weekend, left one person dead and three others shot, Winston-Salem police said. Police received the first call at about 9:45 p.m. on November 7, Forsyth County EMS took three victims to hospital, and investigators had not released the dead person's identity, said whether any victim was a student, or whether the two incidents were connected.

stories.headline: Bacon Wins Speaker Bid, Making History as Colorado's First Black Woman to Lead House
stories.summary: State Rep. Jennifer Bacon of Denver has won her Democratic colleagues' backing to become the next speaker of the Colorado House, making her the first Black woman to lead the chamber. Bacon, the assistant majority leader, defeated Rep. Andrew Boesenecker in the caucus vote and will lead a chamber where Democrats hold 49 of 65 seats after the midterms.

stories.headline: Coco Gauff vs Jessica Pegula headlines WTA Finals opening day: Draw, format, everything to know
stories.summary: The 2026 WTA Finals open on Sunday, November 8 at Indian Wells with Coco Gauff facing Jessica Pegula in the headline match of day one, the pair tied 5-5 in their head-to-head with Gauff winning both meetings this year, at Wimbledon and in the Cincinnati final. Defending champion and world No. 1 Elena Rybakina has withdrawn for an undisclosed medical reason and is replaced by Marta Kostyuk, and the eight-player round-robin event runs to November 15 with a $10 million prize pool.

stories.headline: Brawl overshadows Arkansas-Pine Bluff’s 35-32 comeback win over Grambling
stories.summary: Arkansas-Pine Bluff's 35-32 comeback win at Grambling State on Saturday was overshadowed by a postgame brawl between players from both teams that took several minutes to bring under control. Grambling apologised the same night, said those involved would face disciplinary action, and UAPB coach Alonzo Hampton called the incident embarrassing; on the field, the Golden Lions rallied from 25-21 down in the fourth quarter behind Jaylen Jennings' touchdown run and DaeDae Allen's 76-yard punt-return score to stay in the SWAC West race at 6-3.

stories.headline: 2026 Election Results Winners and Losers: Catastrophe for the ANC and EFF and good news for the DA, ActionSA, VF Plus, and PA
stories.summary: South Africa's ANC has recorded its worst local election result since 1994, falling to 30.76 percent with 99.95 percent of voting districts counted, down 15 points on 2021, a result secretary-general Fikile Mbalula called catastrophic for the movement. The DA took 24.64 percent, Jacob Zuma's MK Party 9.76 percent and the EFF 6.22 percent, while ActionSA was the biggest gainer at 5.67 percent, and with the DA holding an outright majority only in Cape Town, coalition talks will decide most big-city governments.

stories.headline: Uganda Lady Cranes win 2026 Africa Women's 7s to qualify SVNs 3
stories.summary: Uganda's Lady Cranes won their first Africa Women's Sevens title with a 33-0 win over Tunisia in the final at Nairobi's RFUEA Grounds, Lydia Namabiro scoring a hat-trick, and qualified for World Rugby's SVNS 3 in Dubai in December. Hosts Kenya took third place with a 27-7 bronze-final win over Zimbabwe after losing their semi-final to Uganda, and Zambia beat South Africa for the second time in the tournament to finish fifth.

stories.headline: Kenya’s Rising Lionesses to receive handsome reward after historic gold at Dakar Olympics
stories.summary: Kenya's junior women's rugby sevens team, the Rising Lionesses, will each receive Ksh 250,000 in reward for winning gold at the Dakar Youth Olympic Games, Sports Principal Secretary Elijah Mwangi announced at a dinner for the team on Saturday night. The side's 17-12 win over Australia made them Kenya's first team sport to win an Olympic gold medal, and Mwangi urged the Kenya Rugby Union to build the squad toward the World Rugby Series and a World Cup.

stories.headline: Police seize 454kg of suspected methamphetamine worth Sh3.6bn in Kwale
stories.summary: Kenyan police have seized 454 kilogrammes of suspected methamphetamine valued at about Sh3.6 billion in Kwale County and arrested three foreign nationals, two Tanzanians and a Ugandan woman, in a multi-agency operation against a suspected international drug trafficking network. The National Anti-Narcotics Bureau Coast Region led the operation with Tanzanian agencies after Tanzania arrested 45-year-old Saleh Khamis on November 5 and handed him to Kenyan officers at the Lunga Lunga-Horohoro border, and investigations into the drugs' source and destination are continuing.

stories.headline: Kenya's Dr. Jackson Bett sworn in to AfCFTA dispute settlement appellate body
stories.summary: Dr Jackson Bett of Kenya has been sworn in as a member of the Appellate Body of the African Continental Free Trade Area's Dispute Settlement Body, with AfCFTA Secretary-General Wamkele Mene administering the oath at the secretariat in Accra, Ghana. The appointment helps operationalise the legal machinery for resolving cross-border trade disputes across the AfCFTA market of more than 1.3 billion people, as member states move to eliminate tariffs on 90 percent of tariff lines.

stories.headline: Mahama Allocates GH¢100 Million to Complete Nsawam Prison Remand Block in 2027
stories.summary: President John Dramani Mahama has announced a GH¢100 million allocation in Ghana's 2027 budget to complete the abandoned remand block at Nsawam Medium Security Prison, so that prisoners awaiting trial are held separately from convicted inmates. Mahama, who disclosed the commitment at an Assemblies of God induction ceremony in Accra on Saturday, said construction began under his previous administration and was abandoned after it left office, and that remand prisoners have not been convicted and should not be treated as though they had been.

stories.headline: Kofi Wayo: The Life and Political Journey of Ghana’s Outspoken Politician
stories.summary: Charles Eric Kofi Wayo, the outspoken Ghanaian politician and businessman known as Chuck, has died aged 71 at the Nyaho Medical Centre in Accra after a short illness, his family has confirmed. Wayo rose to prominence contesting the Ayawaso East seat for the NPP in 2000, later founded the United Renaissance Party in 2006 and served on the Energy Commission board before retiring from active politics in 2017 to support rural farmers; funeral arrangements have not yet been announced.

stories.headline: North Carolina Central rallies for wild win at Norfolk State to remain unbeaten in MEAC play
stories.summary: North Carolina Central rallied to beat Norfolk State 29-28 on Saturday, Joshua Jones hitting Mehki Wall for a 26-yard touchdown with 27 seconds left after Norfolk State fumbled the ball back when it only needed to run out the clock. The win kept the Eagles unbeaten in the MEAC at 3-0 and set up a first-place showdown with South Carolina State, while Jones threw for three touchdowns and ran for another and Gino Addison rushed for 174 yards.

stories.headline: AFROTECH™ 2026 SPOTLIGHTS TECHNOLOGY, POLICY AND INNOVATION DURING THIRD DAY IN HOUSTON
stories.summary: AfroTech 2026's programming in Houston spotlighted the intersection of technology, policy, healthcare and business as the conference marked its 10th anniversary, including its inaugural Executive Policy Breakfast on technology's impact on civic engagement and Smart Cities sessions on clean energy and civic innovation. The highlights also covered the HealthStack healthcare programme, with clinical AI and digital health sessions, the Authors Pavilion with Roy Wood Jr., Robin Givhan and Tareasa Johnson, and a Legacy Dinner honouring the Future 50 in partnership with Black Enterprise.

stories.headline: 2026 U-17 WWC: Flamingos beat Japan 2-1 to win historic World Cup title
stories.summary: Nigeria's Flamingos beat Japan 2-1 in Saturday's final at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Rabat to win the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup for the first time, becoming the first African country to lift the trophy. The title capped a turnaround from an opening 2-1 defeat to Poland, after which Nigeria beat Puerto Rico, defending champions North Korea, Mexico, Venezuela and Brazil to reach the final.

stories.headline: Fort Valley State University receives $5.8 million gift, largest donation in university's history
stories.summary: Fort Valley State University has received a $5.8 million donation, the largest gift in the Georgia HBCU's history, in a boost the university says underscores the importance of private philanthropy to HBCU sustainability. The specific allocation of the funds has not yet been detailed, and the gift arrives as HBCUs across the country have intensified fundraising to strengthen their financial positions.

stories.headline: 'Earn Your Leisure' Hosts Troy Millings And Rashad Bilal On Importance Of Collaboration Among New Generation Of Black Wealth Builders
stories.summary: Earn Your Leisure hosts Rashad Bilal and Troy Millings used a live State of Black Business recording on the AFROTECH Conference main stage, alongside Blavity founder Morgan DeBaun, to argue that collaboration, not competition, is how the new generation of Black wealth builders will compound its gains. They pointed to their Sanbra City Project in Accra, Ghana, a 400-acre residential development of at least 600 units built in partnership with local Ghanaian entrepreneurs, as the model in action.

stories.headline: 5 Games to Watch in Week 10 of the HBCU football season
stories.summary: Week 10 of the HBCU football season closes the Division II regular season on Saturday, November 7 with championship places on the line: Virginia Union meets Virginia State and Johnson C. Smith faces Livingstone with CIAA title-game spots at stake, Central State visits Benedict for the remaining SIAC berth, and in the SWAC the division leaders Alabama A&M and Prairie View A&M meet while Arkansas-Pine Bluff tries to stay in a three-way West tie against Grambling State.

stories.headline: Mariga ousted as FKF vice-president following stormy meeting in Meru
stories.summary: Football Kenya Federation vice-president MacDonald Mariga has been expelled from the National Executive Committee along with six other members at a Special General Meeting in Meru, with 65 delegates voting in favour and AFC Leopards chair Boniface Ambani the only one opposed. The meeting, chaired by FKF president Hussein Mohammed, went ahead after a turbulent morning in which police Rapid Deployment Unit officers discharged teargas at the Three Steers Hotel venue, and Mohammed said all seven members had been invited to defend themselves but neither appeared nor sent a representative.

stories.headline: Bank of Ghana Governor reports 41.2% growth in private sector credit and US$8.81bn trade surplus
stories.summary: Bank of Ghana Governor Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama has told Parliament's Committee on Economy and Development that private sector credit grew 41.2 percent in the first half of 2026 as the average lending rate fell from 27 percent to 15.6 percent, after the policy rate was cut from 18 percent to 14 percent and then held. He reported first-quarter GDP growth of 6.4 percent, a trade surplus of US$8.81 billion and a current account surplus of US$5.1 billion, with international reserves of US$12.94 billion covering five months of imports and non-performing loans down from 23.1 percent to 16.1 percent.

stories.headline: Africa Women’s Sevens kicks off in Nairobi without Nigeria
stories.summary: The 2026 Africa Women's Sevens Championship has kicked off at the RFUEA Grounds in Nairobi, bringing together 11 national teams on November 7 and 8 in a tournament that doubles as the Africa qualifier for World Rugby's HSBC SVNS 3 in Dubai. Hosts Kenya open in Pool B against Ghana and Tunisia, while defending champions South Africa, winners of 13 titles, headline Pool A; Nigeria's Lady Stallions are notably absent, which the report attributes to lost continental ranking and continuity rather than a lack of talent.

stories.headline: Akuna Group Advances Commonwealth Creative Economy Partnerships
stories.summary: Sierra Leone and Kenya have signed Statements of Intent with Idris Elba's Akuna Group at CHOGM 2026 in Antigua and Barbuda, becoming founding champions of the Commonwealth Creative Economy Partnership, a voluntary initiative to connect creative talent with skills, investment and markets. Chief Minister David Moinina Sengeh signed for Sierra Leone and Principal Secretary Korir Sing'Oei for Kenya, with Ghana conveying a message of goodwill, and the statement linked the partnership to Akuna and Google's US$1 million From Script to Screen with AI training for filmmakers in five African countries.

stories.headline: 2027: Tinubu Seeks Akwa Ibom Youths’ Support, Announces Approval of Ibom Deep-Sea Port
stories.summary: President Bola Tinubu has announced approval of the long-awaited Ibom Deep-Sea Port in Akwa Ibom State, along with international status for Victor Attah International Airport, during a rally in Uyo on Friday held as part of his working visit and 2027 re-election campaigning. Tinubu granted the requests made by Governor Umo Eno, said the port would bring economic benefits and accelerate development in the state, and had earlier inaugurated the airport's new international terminal.

stories.headline: US advances investment push in DR Congo, eyes critical minerals, transport infrastructure
stories.summary: The United States and the Democratic Republic of Congo have advanced plans to expand American investment under their Strategic Partnership Agreement at the second Joint Steering Committee meeting in Paris, with critical minerals, hydropower and regional transport as the focus. A joint statement said the US International Development Finance Corporation briefed the meeting on its growing DRC investment pipeline amid rising private-sector interest in the country's Strategic Asset Reserve, and the two sides recognised the Lobito Corridor concession agreement as a milestone and discussed next steps for the Grand Inga hydropower project.

stories.source: The Journal of Blacks in Higher Education
stories.headline: Ten HBCUs Receive More Than $97 Million in Combined Federal Defense Funding
stories.summary: Ten HBCUs will share more than $97 million in federal Defense Department funding for STEM research, in an award aimed at helping more of the schools reach R1 status, the highest research classification, currently held among HBCUs only by Howard University. Florida A&M, North Carolina A&T and Morgan State each received $10 million, with Clark Atlanta, Delaware State, the University of the District of Columbia, Fayetteville State, Prairie View A&M and Texas Southern each receiving between $9.78 million and $9.99 million and Jackson State $7.57 million.

stories.headline: RECAP: AfroTech Turns 10: Inside The Conversations And Experiences Shaping The Future Of Black Innovation
stories.summary: ESSENCE's recap of AfroTech's 10th anniversary conference in Houston found Black innovation moving from breaking in to shaping what comes next, with artificial intelligence the defining theme, from Microsoft's House of Black TechXcellence and GitHub Copilot sessions to a Policy Breakfast held the morning after the midterms. The recap also highlighted the Authors Stage, LinkedIn and Verizon activations, and conference programming on ownership, access and who benefits from technological change.

stories.headline: HBCU Alumni Make History With Major Wins In 2026 Midterm Elections
stories.summary: Graduates of historically Black colleges and universities won historic victories across the 2026 midterms, Capital B News reporting carried by Black Enterprise shows: Florida A&M graduate Keisha Lance Bottoms became the first Black woman elected governor in U.S. history in Georgia, Spelman graduate Adrienne Adams became New York's first Black woman elected lieutenant governor, and Florida A&M's Milton Potter was elected lieutenant governor of the U.S. Virgin Islands. HBCU alumni also won in Congress, with Florida A&M's Oliver Gilbert III in Florida and Howard's Donna Miller in Illinois, while Talladega's Nikema Williams and Howard Law's Letitia James won re-election in Georgia and New York.

stories.headline: Black voter turnout helped contribute to major Democratic wins
stories.summary: Black voter turnout helped power the Democratic midterm wave, Emory University political scientist Andra Gillespie told NPR, pointing to Georgia data showing African American, Latino and Asian American turnout up on 2022 while white turnout fell, making Black voters a larger share of the 2026 electorate. Exit polls also showed Black men swinging back toward Democrats after 2024, with the economy the top issue for Black voters in Southern states, and Gillespie argued that Republican-drawn maps after the Supreme Court's Voting Rights Act decision ended up creating districts Democrats could compete in during a wave year.

stories.headline: DJ's Alliance launches statewide campaign to support suicide loss survivors
stories.summary: Delaware-based nonprofit DJ's Alliance has launched Delaware Goes Teal & Purple, a month-long statewide campaign under the theme Stigma is out. Hope is in, offering a free bilingual Community Action Toolkit to help individuals, schools, workplaces and faith communities support suicide loss survivors and challenge stigma. The campaign runs through four weekly themes and builds toward International Survivors of Suicide Loss Day on November 21 and the organisation's third annual Survivor Day Trot 5K in Dover on November 22.

stories.headline: LinkedIn Is Addressing AI Slop And Finding Ways To Drive Authentic Engagements, Says Senior Product Manager Travis Hutchinson
stories.summary: LinkedIn senior product manager Travis Hutchinson told an AFROTECH Conference session on getting discovered in the LinkedIn feed that the platform is pushing back against low-quality AI-generated content, describing a general quality push across its classifiers and feed ranking alongside new features such as pinned comments. LinkedIn data shared on the panel said nearly 700 million comments are viewed daily, and that more than a quarter of Black professionals credit commenting, sharing and joining professional conversations with access to additional opportunities, the highest share of any racial or ethnic group surveyed.

stories.headline: Six Ebola patients recover as Kenya records 18 days without new infection
stories.summary: Kenya has discharged a sixth Ebola patient, leaving only one person under treatment, after 18 consecutive days without a new infection, the Ministry of Health has said on Day 32 of the outbreak. Director-General for Health Dr Patrick Amoth said confirmed cases remain at nine, all linked to a single chain of transmission with no new case since October 19, while 66 contacts have completed the mandatory 21-day monitoring and 52 more are expected to finish by November 11; a 42-day countdown to declaring the outbreak over can only begin once the last patient is discharged.

stories.headline: ANC on course for worst electoral showing yet
stories.summary: South Africa's African National Congress is on course for its worst electoral showing yet in this week's municipal elections, holding 31.9 percent support with 70 percent of ballots counted, down from 45.6 percent in the last local elections in 2021, as voters punished it over water and power outages and potholed roads. The Democratic Alliance stood at 24.6 percent, Jacob Zuma's MK Party at 9 percent and the Economic Freedom Fighters at 6.2 percent, with the DA on track to retain Cape Town, no party leading outright in the other seven big metros, and final results and seat allocations expected over the weekend.

stories.headline: Mississippi Votes Still Being Counted in Senate Nail-Biter After Democrats Take Control of Congress
stories.summary: Mississippi's Senate race remains too tight to call, with Democratic challenger Scott Colom leading Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith 49 percent to 48.9 percent, a gap of 1,813 votes with 96 percent of ballots counted, as Democrats hope for their first Senate victory in the state since 1982. The NAACP has deployed national legal, policy and field staff to help ensure every eligible vote is counted, and about 3,600 absentee-by-mail ballots were still outstanding within the state's receipt window.

stories.headline: Democratic Socialist Nithya Raman Defeats Karen Bass in the Los Angeles Mayor's Race
stories.summary: City Council member Nithya Raman has defeated incumbent Karen Bass in the Los Angeles mayoral race, NBC News projected Thursday, unseating the former six-term congresswoman who was the city's second Black mayor. Bass's term was marked by intense scrutiny over her response to the January 2025 Palisades wildfire, and Raman campaigned against what she called a broken status quo on homelessness and housing; Bass called to congratulate Raman and both pledged a smooth transition.

stories.headline: AVMA Approves First Public HBCU Vet School
stories.summary: The University of Maryland Eastern Shore School of Veterinary Medicine has received a Letter of Reasonable Assurance from the American Veterinary Medical Association Council on Education, allowing it to begin recruiting its inaugural Doctor of Veterinary Medicine class for summer 2027. The school will be the first veterinary school physically located in Maryland and the first at a public HBCU, offering an accelerated three-year, year-round curriculum in a field where just 1.6 percent of U.S. veterinarians were Black in 2025.

stories.headline: Coppin State University Ranks Among Top Five HBCUs for Alumni Earnings
stories.summary: Coppin State University has been ranked No. 4 among HBCUs for alumni earnings in a ranking published by Always College citing the 2026 College Scorecard, reporting median annual earnings of $63,359 for graduates four years after completion. About 64 percent of Coppin's incoming students are first-generation college students, and the Baltimore university recently reported a 30.1 percent enrollment increase for fall 2026, the highest percentage growth in the University System of Maryland.

stories.headline: Two Jackson State University Students Dead and Six Others Injured in Nightclub Shooting
stories.summary: A shooting at a nightclub has killed two Jackson State University students and injured six others, according to reporting from the Mississippi Free Press carried by HBCU.news. The off-campus incident has left the Jackson State community grieving and raised renewed questions about student safety and violence prevention in the spaces around HBCU campuses, where student organizations such as the Divine Nine often become pillars of support after a tragedy.

stories.headline: Football Falls to Defending HBCU National Champion
stories.summary: South Carolina State beat Howard 35-28 at Greene Stadium on Thursday night, with running back Ricorian Brown rushing for a career-high 143 yards and two touchdowns, including the nine-yard game-winner that capped a seven-play, 71-yard drive late in the fourth quarter. Howard quarterback Isaiah Freeman threw for 233 yards and three touchdowns as the Bison twice rallied to tie the defending Black national champions, who improved to 8-2 overall and 3-0 in the MEAC with their 12th straight conference win.

stories.headline: Film, Music and Fashion Unite as CANEX WKND 2026 Opens in Lagos, Bringing Together Leading African and Diaspora Creatives, Investors
stories.summary: Creative Africa Nexus WKND 2026 has opened in Lagos, running November 5 to 8 under the theme One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World, hosted by Nigeria's federal government and organised by Afreximbank. The four-day gathering spans film, music, fashion, sport, publishing and gastronomy, with a Deal Room and pitch sessions aimed at turning creative talent into businesses, backed by Afreximbank's US$2 billion commitment to Africa's creative industries and participants including Wole Soyinka, Didier Drogba, Jay-Jay Okocha and Davido.

stories.headline: Paul Mackenzie Sentenced to 200 Years in Prison Over Shakahola Deaths
stories.summary: Kenya's High Court in Mombasa has sentenced preacher Paul Mackenzie to a total of 200 years in prison over the Shakahola massacre, handing down two consecutive 100-year terms after he and 28 co-accused were convicted on October 19 on all 191 murder counts. Justice Diana Kavedza classified 183 deaths as murder by starvation, comprising 182 children and one adult, and eight children as victims of direct homicide, found Mackenzie bore primary culpability as leader of the Good News International settlement, and declined the death penalty prosecutors had sought.

stories.headline: Mombasa RFC Secure Multimillion Sponsorship to Boost Push for Kenya Cup Return
stories.summary: Mombasa Sports Club Rugby has secured a Sh4.5 million sponsorship deal with Mitchell Cotts Freight Kenya Limited as title sponsor over three seasons, providing Sh1.5 million a year to support its push to return to the Kenya Cup. The logistics firm steps up from kit sponsor, taking the front-of-shirt position on the club's senior 15s and sevens kits, and the funding will cover travel, accommodation, equipment and match operations plus the club's age-grade community programme ahead of its Kenya Rugby Championship opener against South Coast Pirates on November 21.

stories.headline: SQUIRE Co-Founder And President Dave Salvant Said He Was Asked To Hire Non-Black Executives When He Was Raising Funding
stories.summary: SQUIRE co-founder and president Dave Salvant told the AFROTECH Conference that while raising venture funding for the barbershop management platform, one investor asked the company to hire non-Black executives, a request he said would never be made of a non-Black founder. SQUIRE, which Salvant co-founded after buying and running a Manhattan barbershop to learn the business, is now used by more than 3,000 barbershops with 7.6 million booking clients, is valued at $750 million and raised its Series A through D rounds within 18 months.

stories.headline: Puma Rolls Out New Divine Nine Collection During HBCU Homecoming Season
stories.summary: PUMA has launched a new collection honoring the Divine Nine, the historically Black fraternities and sororities of the National Pan-Hellenic Council, timed to HBCU homecoming season. The initial release covers six of the nine organizations, including Zeta Phi Beta, Sigma Gamma Rho, Phi Beta Sigma and Kappa Alpha Psi, with each group's colors, letters and graphics applied to styles such as the PUMA Suede, Leadcat 2.0 slides, hoodies and T7 track jackets; Delta Sigma Theta, Alpha Kappa Alpha and Alpha Phi Alpha are not in the first release.

stories.headline: Dangote Boosts Africa Plan to $60bn as He Starts New Build
stories.summary: Aliko Dangote has raised his group's pledge to invest in industrialising Africa to $60 billion by the end of the decade as he broke ground on a fuel depot outside Walvis Bay, Namibia. The tank farm is part of a $2.5 billion investment that includes a planned 1,700-kilometre pipeline through Botswana and South Africa, with about four million barrels of storage split between 360 million litres of diesel and 240 million litres of gasoline, and Dangote said the storage facility will take at most 18 months to complete.

stories.headline: M-Pesa, Ethiopia Operations Push Safaricom Half-Year Profit to Sh58.2bn
stories.summary: Safaricom's net profit rose 35.9 percent to Sh58.2 billion in the six months to September, as M-Pesa revenue climbed 13.6 percent to Sh100.1 billion, passing Sh100 billion in a half-year for the first time. Kenya service revenue grew 11.3 percent to Sh216 billion, while the Ethiopia business grew service revenue 71.6 percent to Sh10.6 billion with 15.4 million active customers, and chief executive Peter Ndegwa said the company is targeting EBITDA break-even in Ethiopia by the end of the financial year.

stories.headline: Ghana Reaches IMF Deal on First Review of 36-Month Economic Programme
stories.summary: Ghana and IMF staff have reached a staff-level agreement on the first review of the country's 36-month programme under the Policy Coordination Instrument, a non-financing arrangement, after a mission to Accra from October 22 to November 4 led by Ruben Atoyan; the deal still needs IMF Management and Executive Board approval. The Fund cited real GDP growth of 6.2 percent in the first half of 2026 and inflation of 5.5 percent in October, while urging Ghana to rebuild foreign exchange reserves that have fallen in recent months.

stories.headline: New Malaria Drug to Be Unveiled to Stay Ahead of Resistance
stories.summary: Kenya will receive the first batch of a new malaria drug, artesunate-pyronaridine (ASPY), in November under the Kenya-United States government partnership on health, with four counties set to begin using it in January. The drug will be used alongside artemether-lumefantrine, the treatment Kenya has relied on for 20 years, as part of a multiple first-line therapies approach, with Baringo among the rollout counties, intended to preserve the effectiveness of anti-malaria medicines as resistance concerns grow.

stories.headline: Doug Williams Up for Pro Football Hall of Fame
stories.summary: Grambling State legend Doug Williams has been named one of five remaining candidates in the contributor category for the Pro Football Hall of Fame's Class of 2027, alongside Robert Kraft, Virginia McCaskey, John Wooten and Ralph Hay. Williams was the first Black quarterback drafted in the first round and the first to start and win a Super Bowl, and a subcommittee meets November 17 to advance one of the five to the full selection committee.

stories.headline: Coco Gauff Donates Another $150,000 to UNCF, Taking Her Total Contribution to $250,000 for HBCU Students
stories.summary: Tennis star Coco Gauff has donated another $150,000 to the United Negro College Fund, bringing her total giving to UNCF to $250,000 for scholarships supporting HBCU student athletes who compete in tennis. The Coco Gauff Scholarship Program has already helped 10 student athletes at six institutions, including Alabama A&M, Clark Atlanta, Howard, Livingstone and Tuskegee, and UNCF has not yet announced the next application window.

stories.headline: AfroTech 2026 Kicks Off 10th Anniversary Celebration in Houston, Bringing Together Leaders in AI, Technology, Business and Entrepreneurship
stories.summary: AfroTech 2026 has officially kicked off in Houston, marking the conference's 10th anniversary with a week of programming for entrepreneurs, executives, technology professionals, creators and investors. Day one featured an AI Edge Training Summit, a Human Centered AI for Leaders Summit and Idea Hour pitch sessions with Rachel Rodgers and Arlan Hamilton, and the conference runs through Friday, November 6 with programming on healthcare innovation, policy, smart cities and the creator economy.

stories.headline: DA Claims Historic Milestone as Black Voter Support Surpasses 1 Million
stories.summary: South Africa's Democratic Alliance says more than one million Black South Africans voted for it in the 2026 local government elections, a first in the party's history, putting it ahead of the Economic Freedom Fighters among Black voters on its internal modelling and parallel vote tabulation. Federal Council first deputy chair Ashor Sarupen said the party forecast about 15 percent support in Gauteng townships and 10 percent in Cape Town townships plus gains in rural KwaZulu-Natal and the Eastern Cape, while noting the figures still await certification by the Electoral Commission of South Africa.

stories.headline: Court Sacks Mark-Led ADC Leadership, Nullifies Atiku's Candidacy
stories.summary: Nigeria's Federal High Court in Abuja has nullified the African Democratic Congress leadership led by former Senate President David Mark, invalidating its decisions including the primary that made former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar the party's presidential candidate for the 2027 elections. Justice Peter Lifu ruled the caretaker committee's emergence violated the ADC constitution and electoral law, voided all of the party's 2027 nominations, and directed INEC not to recognise decisions of the disputed leadership; the party says it will appeal.

stories.headline: History Made! Nigeria's Flamingos Reach First-Ever FIFA U-17 World Cup Final
stories.summary: Nigeria's Flamingos beat Brazil 3-1 in Morocco on November 4 to reach the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup final for the first time, becoming the first African nation to reach the tournament's final and improving on their third place finish in 2022. Queen Joseph opened the scoring in the 56th minute and Awawu Bashiru added goals in the 71st and 80th minutes before Brazil's late consolation, and Nigeria will face Japan in the final on Saturday, November 7 in Rabat.

stories.headline: ECOWAS Holds Regional Meetings in Ghana to Strengthen Copyright Protection, Recover Cultural Heritage
stories.summary: ECOWAS has held regional meetings in Accra, Ghana from November 3 to 5 on strengthening copyright protection for creators and recovering West Africa's cultural heritage, opened by Ghana's Minister for Tourism, Culture and the Creative Arts, Abla Dzifa Gomashie. Experts validated a study on private copying remuneration across member states, and the regional committee on repatriation worked on the 2027-2031 action plan for returning cultural property to its countries of origin, with UEMOA and WIPO also taking part.

stories.headline: Inaugural Women's Health Ecosystem Forum Seeks to Advance African-Led Research and Innovation
stories.summary: The inaugural Women's Health Ecosystem Forum has run in Kenya from November 2 to 5, convened by the LEA-WH Fellowship with the Kenya Medical Research Institute and the U.S. National Academy of Medicine to turn African-led women's health research into products, investment and practical solutions. KEMRI leaders said conditions such as endometriosis, menstrual disorders and menopause remain under-researched and underfunded, and the fellowship's first cohort brings together researchers and innovators from nine African countries, funded by the Gates Foundation.

stories.headline: Africa FX: Ugandan and Nigerian Currencies on Front Foot
stories.summary: Traders expect Uganda's and Nigeria's currencies to strengthen against the dollar in the coming week while Ghana's cedi and Kenya's shilling stay little changed and Zambia's kwacha weakens, according to Reuters' weekly Africa FX survey. Nigeria's naira was quoted at 1,346 on the official market as global risk sentiment improved after the U.S. midterm elections, Ghana's cedi traded at 11.67 to the dollar, and Kenya's shilling held at 129.85 to 130.05 per dollar.

stories.headline: In The AI Era, Dr. Timnit Gebru Says The World Should Not Accept The Devaluing Of Black People - 'Technology Needs To Work For Us'
stories.summary: Dr. Timnit Gebru, founder of the Distributed Artificial Intelligence Research Institute, told the AFROTECH Conference's Human Cost of Smarter Systems session on November 3 that Black communities should not accept being devalued in the pursuit of AI innovation. She urged transparency about the datasets behind AI systems, pointed to the low-paid data workers who build them and to harms such as facial-recognition misidentification and data-center pollution in Memphis, arguing that technology needs to work for the people it affects.

stories.headline: FAMU's Oliver Gilbert Wins Florida's 24th District, Heading to Washington to Succeed Frederica Wilson
stories.summary: Florida A&M alumnus and Miami-Dade County commissioner Oliver Gilbert won Florida's 24th Congressional District on Tuesday night, defeating Republican Te Mayonna Brown to succeed retiring Rep. Frederica Wilson, a Fisk University graduate who had endorsed him. Gilbert, a former mayor of Miami Gardens, Florida's largest majority-Black city, won the decisive August Democratic primary with about 34 percent against state Sen. Shevrin Jones and will be sworn in when the new Congress convenes in January.

stories.headline: Nevada Attorney General Aaron Ford Beats Republican Incumbent for Governor
stories.summary: Nevada Attorney General Aaron Ford unseated Republican Gov. Joe Lombardo in one of the country's most competitive governor's races, according to an Associated Press race call, resolving the one Black governor's race left undecided on election night. Ford, previously Nevada's first Black Senate majority leader and attorney general, will become the first Black governor of a state west of the Mississippi River, and he has pledged to revive bills Lombardo vetoed, including limits on corporate home buying and state adoption of Medicaid negotiated drug prices.

stories.headline: Prairie View A&M's Eric Zachery Named Semifinalist for Aeneas Williams Award
stories.summary: Prairie View A&M junior defensive back Eric Zachery has been named one of 10 semifinalists for the 2026 Aeneas Williams Award, which honors the top defensive back in Division I HBCU football. The Dallas native has recorded 39 tackles, four pass breakups and 2.5 tackles for loss through nine games, and he is one of eight SWAC players on the semifinalist list, with three finalists to be announced December 1 and the winner on December 10.

stories.source: The Journal of Blacks in Higher Education
stories.headline: Higher Education Gifts or Grants of Interest to African Americans
stories.summary: The Journal of Blacks in Higher Education's latest grants roundup includes a $496,376 National Science Foundation award to Winston-Salem State University faculty to build teaching units on AI cybersecurity attacks, an $893,779 NSF grant joining Southern University and Grambling State to study the health effects of tire-wear pollution, and a $1.2 million federal TRIO grant for Elizabeth City State University to serve 850 adults a year across seven North Carolina counties. Coppin State University received $1,185,000 to prepare 20 special education teachers, and Tuskegee University received $595,217 to modernize its biology and chemistry teaching laboratories.

stories.headline: Helium Health Awarded Google.org Funding to Deploy Clinical AI for Maternal Healthcare
stories.summary: Nigerian health technology company Helium Health has received a $2.5 million Google.org grant, as the only Nigerian organisation among 15 global recipients of the $30 million Google.org Impact Challenge: AI for Government Innovation, to deploy clinical AI into primary maternal healthcare. Its HeliumMum programme uses AI to help pregnant women identify risks early and connect with providers using electronic medical records and clinical decision support across Lagos, Delta, Kano and Oyo states, with Lagos as the launch base, aiming to reach an additional 1.9 million women over three years.

stories.headline: Tuesday's Elections Bring Historic First for Black Governors
stories.summary: For the first time in U.S. history, multiple elected Black governors will serve at the same time: Wes Moore won re-election in Maryland, Byron Donalds became Florida's first Black governor, Keisha Lance Bottoms won in Georgia, and David Crowley won in Wisconsin, making four Black governors chosen on one night. Only three Black governors had ever been elected before, and none served simultaneously, while Nevada's Aaron Ford race was still undecided.

stories.headline: Letitia Plummer Harris County Judge: Spelman Alum Wins
stories.summary: Spelman College alumna and former Houston City Council member Letitia Plummer defeated Orlando Sanchez with about 62 percent of the vote to become the first African American elected to lead Harris County, Texas's most populous county, and the first Muslim to hold the post. As county judge she will lead the Commissioners Court, which oversees the budget, roads, flood control and public health for nearly 5 million people, succeeding Lina Hidalgo in January.

stories.headline: HBCU Students March to the Polls on Election Day
stories.summary: HBCU students marched and rallied on Election Day from Mississippi to North Carolina and Maryland, with Jackson State, North Carolina A&T, Norfolk State and Morgan State students among those turning out after weeks of organizing. North Carolina A&T students walked about 45 minutes to vote after no campus early-voting sites were approved, Jackson State's Blackout Rally carried demands in the Nolan Wells case, and the Vote HBCU program registered more than 800 students at 10 HBCUs in under a month.

stories.headline: Candace Parker Launches HBCU Sports Media Fellowship
stories.summary: WNBA legend Candace Parker has partnered with EICOP, the organization behind HBCU in LA, to launch the Candace Parker Sports and Media Fellowship for current HBCU students pursuing careers in sports, media and broadcasting. Selected fellows will spend next summer in paid internships in Los Angeles, New York or Atlanta, with housing assistance, mentorship, professional development and direct access to industry professionals, and applications are open now.

stories.headline: Four Nigerian-Americans Emerge Victorious in U.S. Midterm Elections
stories.summary: Four Nigerian-Americans won their races in the November 3 U.S. midterm elections: Will Jawando, Junior Ezeonu, Oye Owolewa and Carol Kazeem, across local government and state legislative contests in Maryland, Texas, Washington, DC and Pennsylvania. A fifth Nigerian-American candidate, Segun Adeyina, was still awaiting a result as counting continued, and the wins were held up as a milestone for Nigerian diaspora participation in American public life.

stories.headline: Billionaire Dangote Plans Undersea Fuel Pipeline to Ghana
stories.summary: Aliko Dangote's group plans an undersea pipeline to carry petrol and other refined fuels from its Lekki refinery in Lagos via Apapa, past Benin and Lome in Togo, to Takoradi or Tema in Ghana, broadly following the West African Gas Pipeline route, with construction to begin in 2028 and cost and capacity not yet disclosed. Kenya is separately reviving its long-stalled Turkana to Lamu crude pipeline to supply the refinery Dangote is building on its coast.

stories.headline: Google Plans Nigeria AI Teacher Training for 2027
stories.summary: Google announced on November 4 that its free AI Educator Series teacher training, starting in South Africa, will expand to Nigeria, Kenya and Ghana in 2027, though no Nigerian start date or registration details were given. Separately, Google DeepMind and the non-profit Fab AI will develop Gemma-based lesson-planning, assessment and teacher-coaching tools in Kenya, Ghana and South Africa, funded by Google.org and the Gates Foundation, aiming first to support up to 500 teachers and 15,000 students.

stories.headline: Black Stars Shortlisted for CAF Men's National Team of the Year Award
stories.summary: Ghana's Black Stars have been shortlisted for the CAF Men's National Team of the Year award after collecting four points in a World Cup group with England, Croatia and Panama and reaching the Round of 16, their first knockout appearance since 2010, before losing 1-0 to Colombia. The 10-team shortlist covers every African nation that played at the 2026 World Cup, and the winners will be unveiled on December 7 in Lagos, Nigeria.

stories.headline: Rising Lionesses Stun Australia to Secure Historic Youth Olympic Gold
stories.summary: Kenya's women's rugby sevens team, the Rising Lionesses, beat Australia 17-12 in sudden-death extra time to win gold at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, coming back from 12-5 down with tries from captain Zain Hido and Josephine Kerubo before Michelle Chemtai scored the winner. It is Kenya's first gold of the Dakar Games and the first time an African nation has won rugby sevens gold at either the Olympic or Youth Olympic Games.

stories.headline: Ghana Inflation Rises Less Than Expected in October
stories.summary: Ghana's annual inflation rose for a third straight month to 5.5 percent in October, up from 5.2 percent in September, but came in below the 6.2 percent economists expected and stayed under the central bank's 8 percent target band. Government statistician Alhassan Iddrisu said non-food inflation of 7.9 percent drove roughly three-quarters of the increase, while food inflation eased to 2.8 percent.

stories.headline: Kenya Discharges Five Ebola Patients After Negative Tests
stories.summary: Kenya's Ministry of Health has discharged five Ebola patients after they tested negative and showed no symptoms, while two other patients remain in hospital receiving supportive care. The ministry also released 46 people who had been quarantined as contacts of the country's first confirmed case, and Kenya has reported no new infections in the past two weeks, though surveillance continues after an outbreak that began with a traveller from the Democratic Republic of Congo via Uganda.

stories.headline: Sterling Bank, Ake Festival Put Africa at the Centre of AI Debate
stories.summary: Sterling Bank has renewed its partnership with the Ake Arts and Book Festival, which returns to Lagos on November 19 to 21 for its 14th edition under the theme Native Intelligence, examining how African knowledge passed down for generations relates to the AI systems now shaping daily life. Founder Lola Shoneyin said a machine knows only what it has been fed and has not been fed much of Africa, framing the festival as a debate over whose intelligence the future is built on.

stories.headline: BET President Louis Carr Explains Its Strategy for Staying at the Forefront of Technology and the Creator Economy at AFROTECH 2026
stories.summary: At the AFROTECH Conference's 10th anniversary edition in Houston, BET president Louis Carr, who has been with the company 39 years and became president in December 2025, described how BET uses AI to enhance rather than replace its work, from BET Awards seating and memorial segments to identifying top Black creator influencers. He set out a creator-economy strategy built on social platforms, live events and a YouTube pre-show aimed at younger audiences who do not normally watch linear television.

stories.headline: Chasity Monroe Named CEO of The Mane Choice, Will Champion Efforts in 'Groundbreaking Hair Growth Technology'
stories.summary: Florida A&M alumna Chasity Monroe, who founded Pink Noire, described as Memphis's only Black-owned beauty supply store, has been appointed CEO of natural hair care brand The Mane Choice. She will lead a brand refresh, retail expansion across Target, Walmart, Sally Beauty and Amazon, and new 2027 product lines including wellness regimens and hair growth technology the company is pursuing a patent for, and she was honored at FAMU homecoming as its inaugural Rattler CEO.

stories.headline: STARZ Backs HBCU Film Festival at Howard University With Hollywood Opportunities
stories.summary: STARZ will serve as the inaugural presenting sponsor of the fourth annual HBCU First LOOK Film & TV Festival at Howard University on November 5 to 7, under the theme How to Be the Next. Founded by Howard alumna Sheila Eldridge, the festival drew more than 450 entries to its 2026 Film Challenge, whose winners will share $8,500 plus an internship opportunity, and 12 Howard students are helping produce this year's event.

stories.headline: Ahead of Historic Midterms, HBCUs Are Building a Civic Infrastructure to Last
stories.summary: Student organizers backed by the Andrew Goodman Foundation have built lasting voter-mobilization networks across HBCU campuses in the South ahead of the November 3 midterms, from Southern University’s Second Line to the Polls in Baton Rouge to poll-monitor training at Jackson State and marches at Texas Southern and North Carolina A&T. The work pairs registration drives and rides to the polls with training that organizers say will outlast this election cycle.

stories.headline: Kinsey Marching 100 Gift: FAMU Gets $2M Matching Challenge
stories.summary: Drs. Bernard and Shirley Pooler Kinsey have committed $2 million to Florida A&M’s Marching 100, announced during homecoming, structured as $1.5 million for an endowed scholarship and operations fund plus $500,000 for immediate priorities. The gift launches a 36-month matching challenge that began October 24 and aims to inspire another $2 million from alumni and supporters, with no minimum gift to take part.

stories.headline: 'The Breakfast Club' and 'Native Land Pod' Team Up to Bring Politics to the People on Election Night
stories.summary: The Breakfast Club and Native Land Pod are joining forces for The People’s Election Night, a four-hour live broadcast from 8 p.m. to midnight ET on November 3 breaking down the 2026 midterms. Angela Rye, Bakari Sellers and Andrew Gillum join Charlamagne tha God, DJ Envy and guests including Fat Joe, Nick Cannon and Ed Gordon, with backing from The Root, iHeartMedia, Blavity and REVOLT and a combined reach organizers put at more than 20 million subscribers.

stories.headline: Black Voter Turnout Surges Across the South as 2026 Midterms Approach, Putting GOP on Notice
stories.summary: Early-voting figures show Black voters across the South, from North Carolina and Georgia to Florida and Louisiana, casting ballots at rates above the broader electorate ahead of the November 3 midterms, with more than 160,000 additional ballots compared with the same point in 2022. Organizers and strategists link the surge in part to fights over redistricting maps that critics say dilute Black voting power.

stories.headline: From Nigeria to Ethiopia, Seven Candidates With African Ancestry Eye US Congress
stories.summary: Seven candidates with roots in Nigeria, Ghana, Egypt, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Liberia and Somalia are seeking seats in the U.S. Congress in the midterms, in what is expected to be the most expensive midterm cycle in U.S. history at over $11 billion in ad spending. First-time candidates Adrian Boafo, Melat Kiros and Ndidiamaka Okpareke join Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed, while incumbents Ilhan Omar, Joe Neguse and Gabe Amo seek re-election.

stories.headline: Gold Fields Pledges $500,000 to Ghana's Black Challenge Amputee Football Team
stories.summary: Gold Fields Ghana has committed $500,000 over two years to the Black Challenge, Ghana’s amputee national football team, as they prepare for the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico from November 13 to 22. The pledge sits inside a wider $5 million Gold Fields sponsorship agreement with the Ghana Football Association, and France’s ambassador to Ghana also promised logistics support for the team, who face Angola, Colombia and Iraq in Group D.

stories.headline: NHRC and TANGO Engage Gambians in Diaspora on National Development and Reform Agenda
stories.summary: The Gambia’s National Human Rights Commission and the Association of Non-Governmental Organisations convened a diaspora engagement on October 31 at the Sir Dawda Kairaba Jawara International Conference Centre in Banjul, backed by the EU and UNDP. Panels covered governance, transitional justice, security sector reform, investment and electoral participation, with officials stressing that Gambians abroad should help shape the reform agenda through their remittances, skills and networks.

stories.headline: Nigeria and China Sign $30 Million Agreement on Grassroots Development Projects
stories.summary: Nigeria and China have signed a 200 million yuan (about $30 million) grant agreement in Abuja to fund community-focused development projects under China’s Small but Beautiful initiative and Nigeria’s Renewed Hope Ward Development Plan. Ambassador Yu Dunhai noted that 2026 marks 55 years of diplomatic relations, with bilateral trade reaching $18 billion in the first half of the year and Nigerian exports to China up 80 percent under a zero-tariff policy.

stories.headline: Attackers Ambush Police Convoy in Nigeria's Zamfara State, Killing at Least Eight
stories.summary: Attackers ambushed a police convoy near Gidan-Giye village in Nigeria’s northwestern Zamfara state on Tuesday, killing at least eight security personnel: five police officers and three members of the state-backed Community Protection Guard. Police said the attackers fired on a bus carrying the team, seized five AK-47 rifles and abducted some officers, while seven others were rescued and two wounded officers were taken for treatment.

stories.headline: Edinburgh Heat-Protection Tech Firm Draconite Wins £25,000 at KPMG's Black Entrepreneurs' Awards
stories.summary: Edinburgh-based Draconite, founded by inventor Dr Alisha Fuller-Armah, was named Most Promising Small Business at KPMG UK’s Black Entrepreneurs’ Awards, winning £25,000 for its heat-protection material with applications in aerospace, defence, electric vehicles and construction. Four winners were chosen from 12 finalists and more than 140 entrants, including Creative Nature, BEAME and the Black British Initiative, and all finalists join a 12-month acceleration programme.

stories.headline: Morgan State Breaks Enrollment Record at 12,119 Students While Pursuing a Historic Public HBCU Medical School
stories.summary: Morgan State University has passed 12,000 students for the first time, reporting 12,119 students for fall 2026, up 5 percent in its sixth straight enrollment record and making it the nation’s third-largest HBCU, with Black male enrollment up 10.3 percent to 3,613. The Baltimore university is also developing its own nonprofit M.D. program, backed by a $1.75 million Robert Wood Johnson Foundation grant, which would be the first medical school operated by a public HBCU.

stories.headline: Alabama A&M Student Wins Grand Prize for Internably, a Networking Platform for Student Interns
stories.summary: Bryson Hannah, a 21-year-old Alabama A&M mechanical engineering student, won the grand prize at the 2026 HBCU Business Pitch Competition during Magic City Classic week for Internably, his platform connecting student interns by city, company and university. Hannah received $4,000 plus $1,000 in earlier-round funding to develop the app ahead of a November iOS launch, in a competition that drew 51 teams from ten Alabama HBCUs pitching for a share of $20,000.

stories.headline: UMES Opens Applications for First Doctor of Veterinary Medicine Program at a Public HBCU
stories.summary: The University of Maryland Eastern Shore has opened applications for the inaugural class of its Doctor of Veterinary Medicine program, Maryland’s first in-state veterinary school and the first at a public HBCU, with the three-year program set to begin in summer 2027. The school notes that just 1.6 percent of U.S. veterinarians were Black in 2025, and applications are due January 15, 2027.

stories.headline: Ghana Rugby Eagles Women Arrive in Kenya Ahead of 2026 Africa Women's Sevens
stories.summary: Ghana’s women’s rugby sevens team, the Rugby Eagles, have arrived in Nairobi for the 2026 Africa Women’s Sevens on November 7-8 at the RFUEA Grounds, where 11 nations will compete for continental honours and a World Rugby SVNS 3 qualification spot. Ghana, ranked seventh in Africa, are drawn in Pool B with hosts Kenya, Tunisia and Egypt.

stories.headline: Black Congressman Shomari Figures Runs Strongly in Gerrymandered Alabama District
stories.summary: Rep. Shomari Figures is mounting a strong re-election fight in Alabama's 2nd Congressional District after the Republican-led legislature redrew it to cut its Black voting-age share from 48 to 40 percent following the Supreme Court's Voting Rights Act decision. Figures has rallied Black voters in Montgomery and Tuskegee while campaigning on food, fuel and fertilizer costs in conservative areas, and ad spending in his race against Rhett Marques has climbed to nearly $10 million.

stories.headline: Hakeem Jeffries Won't Rule Out Impeaching Trump if Democrats Win the House
stories.summary: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries told ABC News that Democrats have ruled nothing in and nothing out on impeaching President Donald Trump if they win the House in Tuesday's midterms, while keeping their focus on the cost of living. Democrats need a net gain of three seats for a majority, and a win would put Jeffries in line to become the first Black Speaker in American history.

stories.headline: Columbia Weighs Task Force to Protect African American Heritage Trail Properties
stories.summary: Columbia's City Council was set to consider creating a Mayor's Task Force for the African American Heritage Trail at its November 2 meeting, to review trail sites and recommend which should receive historic preservation overlay zoning. Only five Columbia properties currently carry that protection, and the council was also to hear an update on the historic McKinney Building and its Jazz Age connections.

stories.headline: Dr. Gail Jhonson Releases New Smooth Jazz Single 'Looking Up'
stories.summary: Composer, pianist and educator Dr. Gail Jhonson, founding musical director of Norman Brown's band and co-founder of the all-female ensemble Jazz in Pink, has released a new smooth jazz single called Looking Up. The instrumental pairs her piano with Guy Stevenson's guitar and was produced by Burnie Stevenson, adding to a career of more than 40 years and eight CDs.

stories.headline: Johnson Scores Twice but Oakwood Falls 4-2 to Tougaloo in HBCUAC Men's Soccer
stories.summary: Roger Johnson II scored both Oakwood goals, including the Ambassadors' first lead of the season, but Tougaloo won the HBCU Athletic Conference men's soccer match 4-2 on Sunday behind a hat trick from Helix Owusu. The loss eliminated Oakwood from tournament contention and closed its season at 0-8 overall.

stories.headline: Akuna Group and Google Launch Free $1 Million AI Filmmaking Programme for Creators in Five African Countries
stories.summary: Akuna Learning, the education arm of Idris Elba's Akuna Group, has opened applications for a tuition-free AI filmmaking programme run with Google and backed by $1 million, open to creators in Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Sierra Leone and South Africa until November 15. The year-long programme starts with a 12-week online academy in early 2027, and selected teams go on to receive mentoring and production funding while keeping ownership of their films.

stories.headline: Facebook Partners With Funke Akindele to Celebrate Nigerian Storytelling Through 'The Four' Premieres
stories.summary: Facebook has partnered with Nollywood filmmaker Funke Akindele to support the London world premiere and Lagos homecoming premiere of her new film The Four. The collaboration will spotlight Nigerian creators at home and in the diaspora and how they use the platform to reach younger audiences and share Nigerian stories worldwide.

stories.headline: Kenya Brings International Investigators Together to Tackle Digital and Cross-Border Crime
stories.summary: Kenya has opened a seven-day International Police Association investigations seminar in Nairobi, bringing together law enforcement, banks and security agencies from countries including Nigeria, Japan, the United States and Sri Lanka. Running November 1 to 7 at the National Criminal Investigations Academy, the programme covers digital fraud, cryptocurrency offences, ransomware, asset tracing and human trafficking.

stories.headline: Black Women Invest Brings More Than 20 Investors to Ghana for 2026 Real Estate and Cultural Tour
stories.summary: More than 20 participants joined the Black Women Invest and Seso Global real estate and cultural tour in Accra, touring developments, meeting developers and viewing land after a four-part webinar series on buying in Ghana. The tour produced numerous sales, and the next edition is set for July 18 to 25, 2027, including a Cape Coast visit and a citizenship and residency day.

stories.headline: African Leaders Adopt 19-Point Accra Declaration on Reparations and Economic Integration
stories.summary: African leaders, former presidents and traditional rulers at the third Elevate Africa Convening in Accra adopted a 19-point declaration calling for reparatory justice, return of cultural property, deeper economic integration and easier movement across African borders. Signatories including former Nigerian President Goodluck Jonathan and Sierra Leonean President Julius Maada Bio also urged faster AfCFTA implementation and stronger diaspora return pathways.

stories.headline: Black Census Finds Just 3 Percent Trust Federal Government Ahead of Midterms
stories.summary: Early findings from Black Futures Lab's 2026 Black Census, based on 6,287 responses from all 50 states, found only 3 percent of respondents trust the federal government and 3 percent trust elected officials overall, while trust in Black elected officials stood at 23 percent. Respondents still planned to vote in the midterms and backed policies including affordable college at 90 percent and reparations at 84 percent.

stories.headline: Marcia Ann Gillespie, Pioneering Editor of ESSENCE and Ms., Dies at 82
stories.summary: Marcia Ann Gillespie, who joined the new ESSENCE magazine in 1970 and became its editor-in-chief at 26, has died at 82, with her death announced on October 31. She later led Ms. magazine as the first Black woman to serve as editor-in-chief of a mainstream American magazine, and she co-authored the authorized biography Maya Angelou: A Glorious Celebration.

stories.headline: Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games Open in Senegal, a First Olympic Event on African Soil
stories.summary: The Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games opened on Saturday at Abdoulaye Wade Stadium in Diamniadio, declared open by President Bassirou Diomaye Faye as the first Olympic event ever staged in Africa. Some 2,655 athletes aged 14 to 17 from 204 delegations will compete in 153 medal events across 25 sports in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly through November 13.

stories.headline: El-Sayed and Rogers Court Black and Jewish Voters in Tight Michigan Senate Race
stories.summary: Republican Mike Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed are both courting Black voters in metro Detroit in the closing days of Michigan's Senate race to succeed Gary Peters. Pollsters say El-Sayed needs very high Black turnout and support in Detroit, Wayne and Oakland counties to win statewide, while Rogers has opened a Detroit office, visited Black churches and launched a Democrats for Rogers coalition.

stories.headline: Angel Reese Makes WNBA Finals Debut With Atlanta Dream, Starring on Court and in Tunnel Looks
stories.summary: In her first season with the Atlanta Dream, Angel Reese won Defensive Player of the Year and recorded three straight double-doubles in her first WNBA Finals, though the Dream lost in seven games to the Golden State Valkyries. USA TODAY also tracked her seven Finals tunnel looks, including a Game 5 all-black outfit centered on a Protect Black Women T-shirt.

stories.headline: Ghana's President Mahama Welcomes UK Shift Toward Reparatory Justice Dialogue
stories.summary: President John Dramani Mahama welcomed the United Kingdom's openness to a formal apology and structured dialogue over its role in the transatlantic slave trade, calling it a significant step toward reparatory justice. As African Union Champion on Reparations, he set out five priorities including a formal apology, action on systemic racism, investment, restitution of stolen cultural heritage, and development partnerships.

stories.headline: Nigerian Diaspora Social Workers Warn UK Child Protection Rules Are Splitting Families
stories.summary: The Association of Nigerian Social Workers in the UK warned that clashes between customary Nigerian parenting practices, including corporal punishment, and British child protection law are leading more Nigerian immigrant families to lose custody of their children. The group petitioned the Nigeria High Commission in London to set up early-intervention desks, legal navigation help and community safeguarding clinics with certified diaspora social workers.

stories.headline: Governance Fell in 23 African Countries Over Past Decade, Mo Ibrahim Index Finds
stories.summary: The 2026 Ibrahim Index of African Governance, released October 31 in Cairo, found overall governance was worse in 23 African countries in 2025 than in 2016, with security, rights and political participation sliding even as infrastructure and economic opportunity improved. Seychelles ranked first, while Burkina Faso and Nigeria recorded the steepest falls.

stories.headline: Two Suspected Ebola Cases in Nigeria Test Negative, Health Authorities Say
stories.summary: Nigeria's disease control centre said samples from two suspected Ebola cases in the country's northeast tested negative after two rounds of testing, and the patients had been isolated while contacts were traced. Nigeria's only confirmed case remains a Swiss woman who travelled via Uganda to Abuja last week and was evacuated to Switzerland with her husband.

stories.headline: FAME Week Africa Puts African Storytelling, AI and the Business of Entertainment in Focus
stories.summary: FAME Week Africa 2026 in Cape Town, held October 28 to November 1 under the theme The Year of the Creator, focused on investment, distribution and who benefits as African film and television reach global audiences. Panels examined how AI is changing production and ownership, while KwaZulu-Natal showcased its locations and filmmakers to international partners.

stories.headline: Fatma Samoura Joins Final Dakar 2026 Olympic Flame Relay in Senegal
stories.summary: Former FIFA Secretary General Fatma Samoura, the first woman and first African to hold that role, joined the final escort of the Dakar 2026 Olympic Flame ahead of the Youth Olympic Games opening on October 31. The 47-day relay covered more than 3,650 kilometres across all 14 regions of Senegal, as the country prepared to host the first Olympic event staged on African soil.

stories.headline: One Dead, Several Wounded in Shooting After Magic City Classic in Birmingham
stories.summary: A shooting near Legion Field at about 7:50 p.m. on October 31, after Alabama A&M beat Alabama State 31-28 in the 85th Magic City Classic, left at least one person dead and several others wounded. Birmingham police suspended all tailgating, ordered people to leave the stadium property, and asked the public to share video footage from the incident.

stories.headline: Delaware State Rallies From 17 Down to Stun Norfolk State 36-33 at the Linc
stories.summary: Delaware State came back from 17 points down late in the third quarter to beat Norfolk State 36-33 at Lincoln Financial Field on October 31, in a matchup of HBCU teams coached by former Eagles DeSean Jackson and Michael Vick. Quarterback Marqui Adams threw four touchdown passes and a walk-off 35-yard field goal sealed the Hornets' win before a paid crowd of 32,567.

stories.headline: Judge Rejects SpaceX Bid to Dismiss NAACP Lawsuit Over Memphis-Area Data Center Pollution
stories.summary: A federal judge in Mississippi rejected SpaceXAI's bid to dismiss an NAACP lawsuit alleging Clean Air Act violations at its Greater Memphis data centers, so the case will proceed. The suit alleges xAI and its subsidiary MZX Tech installed and operated 27 gas turbines in Southaven, Mississippi without an air permit between August and December 2025.

stories.headline: Tracee Ellis Ross, Keke Palmer and Tamara Tunie Win Big at Daytime Emmy Awards
stories.summary: At the 53rd Daytime Emmy Awards in Los Angeles on October 30, Keke Palmer won for Glam Through The Ages, Tracee Ellis Ross won Outstanding Travel and Adventure Program for Solo Traveling with Tracee Ellis Ross, and Tamara Tunie won her first Emmy for Beyond The Gates nearly 40 years after her daytime debut. Tunie's co-star Ambyr Michelle also won an Emerging Talent award.

stories.headline: Black Tech Fest Draws 4,000 People in London as AI Minister Outlines UK Plans
stories.summary: The seventh Black Tech Fest at Tobacco Dock in London drew more than 4,000 people from 30 countries and over 130 speakers from firms including Microsoft, Google DeepMind, OpenAI and Nvidia. Britain's AI minister Kanishka Narayan set out government plans on AI adoption and jobs, including 10,000 digital and technology work placements for young people.

stories.headline: Rep. Jim Clyburn Campaigns in Jackson for Scott Colom, Calling the Senate Race Key for Voting Rights
stories.summary: Rep. Jim Clyburn campaigned in Jackson, Mississippi on October 29 for Senate candidate Scott Colom, arguing the race matters for voting rights after the Supreme Court decision in Louisiana v. Callais. Mississippi's three new majority-Black House districts are expected to face legal challenges, and Clyburn urged Black voters to turn out.

stories.headline: 'Sinners' Inspires Exhibit at California African American Museum
stories.summary: The California African American Museum in Los Angeles has opened Sinners: Sounds That Summon, an exhibition running through March 14, 2027 that explores the power of Black music in American history through Ryan Coogler's film. Centered on the guitar played by Miles Caton's character Sammie Moore, the show includes costumes, props and archival material co-organized with Warner Bros. Archives.

stories.headline: National Park Service Awards $21.8 Million to Preserve African American Civil Rights Sites
stories.summary: The National Park Service awarded $21.8 million in African American Civil Rights grants to 54 preservation projects. Jackson State University received two grants of $750,000 each, for the Alexander Residence Hall and the Stringer Grand Lodge, with Wiley University and Washington College also among the funded sites.

stories.headline: Redistricting Fights Fuel Turnout Among Young Black Voters Across the South
stories.summary: Redistricting efforts ahead of the midterms are coinciding with higher early-vote turnout among young Black voters in Southern states. In Georgia, Black early voting turnout ran about 6 percent higher than at the same point in 2024, even as new maps make some districts less competitive.

stories.headline: Four African Americans Appointed to Administrative Roles at Universities
stories.source: The Journal of Blacks in Higher Education
stories.summary: JBHE's latest appointments roundup names Adriel Hilton as senior advisor to the chancellor at Indiana University Northwest, Jasmine Gurley as senior director of public relations at Howard University, Lauren D. Myers as chief human resources officer at Cheyney University of Pennsylvania, and Damon L. Williams Jr. as vice president of university relations and chief of staff at Adler University.

stories.headline: Choreographer Cynthia Oliver Honored for a Career Exploring Blackness and Afro-Caribbean Culture
stories.source: The Journal of Blacks in Higher Education
stories.summary: Cynthia Oliver, a professor of dance at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign for more than 25 years, has been awarded for her career in choreography. Her experimental dance-theater works explore Blackness, feminism, Black masculinity, and Afro-Caribbean cultures.

stories.headline: Ghana Urged to Build a One-Stop Platform for Diaspora Families Moving Home
stories.summary: Speakers at the inaugural Open D.O.O.R. Dialogues at the University of Ghana called for a single platform covering citizenship, residency, land, housing, and business information for diaspora returnees. The October 30 gathering ran under the theme Come Home. Stay Home. Build Home.

stories.headline: Wray Forward Names 25 Black Entrepreneurs in Its 2026 Powerbook
stories.summary: The UK accelerator Wray Forward named 25 Black entrepreneurs in its 2026 Powerbook for Black History Month and held its first conference in London on October 30. Its new survey found 51 percent of Black founders see access to finance as the main driver of growth, and 55 percent report late payments from customers.

stories.headline: Africa Cup of Nations Returns to a Two-Year Cycle After CAF Reverses Four-Year Plan
stories.summary: The Confederation of African Football voted unanimously to keep the Africa Cup of Nations on its traditional two-year cycle, reversing a plan to move the tournament to every four years. The next edition is set for 2027 in Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda, with further editions in 2028, 2031, and 2033.

stories.headline: 25 Black-Owned Brands Take the Stage at the USBC 360 Founder Showcase in Washington
stories.summary: The U.S. Black Chambers 360 Accelerator brought 25 Black-owned consumer brands to its Founder Showcase and Pitch Competition in Washington, DC on October 29. Founders in beauty, food and beverage, wellness, and lifestyle pitched for visibility and Entrepreneur Awards of up to $50,000.

stories.headline: Ten Black-Led Startups Pitch at DMZ's Black Innovation Summit in Toronto
stories.summary: Ten Black-led startups pitched for a share of $170,000 at Toronto Metropolitan University's sixth annual Black Innovation Summit. The event noted that Black-led startups received just 0.15 percent of Canadian venture capital last year.

stories.headline: Nigeria Postpones Launch of AGLOFEST, Its Planned Global Black Diaspora Festival
stories.summary: The planned October 30 launch of AGLOFEST, a global festival for the Black diaspora that President Bola Tinubu was set to unveil in Abuja, has been postponed indefinitely. The festival plan included a Black Diaspora Economic Forum aimed at investment and cultural exchange.

stories.headline: Nollywood-Africa in Diaspora Film and Food Festival Launched in Accra
stories.summary: The Nollywood-Africa in Diaspora Film and Food Festival launched at the W.E.B. Du Bois Centre in Accra on October 29. The festival itself is set for March 12-13, 2027, linking filmmakers and food culture across Ghana, Nigeria, and the diaspora.

stories.headline: 26 Nigerian Startups Meet 16 Investors in Lagos Connection Drive Backed by Google for Startups
stories.summary: Magna Collective's Investor Connection Drive matched 26 Nigerian startups with 16 venture investors across 61 pre-arranged meetings in Lagos on October 27, backed by Google for Startups, the UK-Nigeria Tech Hub, and the Office for Nigerian Digital Innovation. Nigerian startups raised $635 million in the first nine months of 2026, more than double the same period in 2025.

stories.headline: BeyGOOD Foundation Awards $25,000 to Camp HBCYouth
stories.summary: Beyonce's BeyGOOD Foundation awarded $25,000 to Camp HBCYouth, a seven-week summer camp that introduces kindergarten through fifth-grade students to HBCU campuses. Founded in 2021, the camp has served about 2,000 students, and early enrollment for the next season opens November 9.

stories.headline: Study: Discrimination at the Doctor's Office May Keep Black Men From Talking About Diabetes
stories.summary: A Texas A and M study of 1,225 Black men living with Type 2 diabetes found that men who experienced discrimination in medical settings were less likely to talk about their diabetes, a pattern linked to how the disease is managed day to day.

stories.headline: Motherwell Celebrates Black History Month With Our Stories, Our Communities, Our Future
stories.summary: Residents, school pupils, and community groups in Motherwell, Scotland marked Black History Month with music, art, drama, and an original songwriting session. North Lanarkshire Council recently passed a cross-party motion committing to properly recognize Black History Month each year.

stories.headline: Breast Cancer Gaps for Black Women Track Poverty and Social Conditions, Not Ancestry, Study Finds
stories.summary: New research published in Cancer Research found that differences in breast cancer outcomes for Black women are tied to socioeconomic factors and poverty burden, including collagen architecture and immune response, rather than to ancestry itself.

stories.headline: Black Adults in Disadvantaged Neighborhoods Less Likely to Be Diagnosed With AFib, Study Finds
stories.summary: A JAMA Network Open study of 504,876 greater Philadelphia residents found Black adults in disadvantaged neighborhoods were less likely than white adults to be diagnosed with atrial fibrillation, pointing to gaps in detection that can delay stroke prevention.

stories.headline: What We Need to Know: Midterms, Health Coverage, HBCU Homecoming, and the NBA Tip-Off
stories.summary: Sybil Wilkes's weekly roundup for Black families covers the November 3 midterm elections, breast cancer awareness and the higher mortality rate Black women face, open enrollment deadlines for Medicare and ACA plans, HBCU homecoming season, and the start of the NBA season.

stories.headline: First Black Woman to Register a Drone Academy in Texas Builds a Path for Black Drone Entrepreneurs
stories.summary: Steffanie Rivers, founder and CEO of TCB Drones and the first Black woman to register a drone academy in Texas, has launched the Next Level Drone Accelerator to help certified pilots turn their skills into businesses. A licensing program in development would let qualified entrepreneurs open TCB Drones academies in their own cities, with Savannah, Georgia as the pilot market.

stories.headline: Africa and African Diaspora Conference Meets in South Africa Under the Theme The Return to Africa
stories.summary: African leaders, scholars, faith leaders, and diaspora representatives gathered in Ekurhuleni from October 26 to 30 for the second Africa and African Diaspora Conference. With speakers including Thabo Mbeki and Ellen Johnson Sirleaf, the meeting aimed to turn shared history into practical cooperation on reparations, investment, and representation.

stories.headline: Volunteers Restore Knoxville's Historic Mysterious Ten Cemetery
stories.summary: Volunteers in Knoxville, Tennessee are restoring the historic Mysterious Ten Cemetery, a burial ground with graves dating to about 1900, with support from a Tennessee America 250 grant. A rededication ceremony was scheduled for October 31, 2026.

stories.headline: Target Commits $500,000 to REVOLT's Bet on Black, Featuring HBCU Student Founders
stories.summary: Target committed $500,000 to season six of REVOLT's Bet on Black pitch series, which this year features only HBCU student founders. Every participating founder receives a share of the fund and keeps full ownership of their company.

stories.headline: ESSENCE Honors Four Leaders at Its Black Women in Business Luncheon
stories.summary: ESSENCE's Black Women in Business Luncheon honored Tamron Hall, Anifa Mvuemba, Ayiko Broyard, and Sarah Curtis Henry. The luncheon was held at Villa Lewaro, the Hudson Valley estate built by Madam C.J. Walker.

stories.headline: Bethune-Cookman University Secures Nearly $5.2 Million in Its First Federal Nursing Grants
stories.summary: Bethune-Cookman University won $5,169,169 in its first-ever grants from the federal Health Resources and Services Administration, funding a nursing student success pathway and a program for working healthcare professionals. A separate $250,000 Florida appropriation will support dual-enrollment nursing credits for high school students.

stories.headline: Camden Launches Its Biggest Black History Season Yet in London
stories.summary: The London Borough of Camden opened its Black History Season with its largest programme yet, spanning exhibitions, Caribbean cook-ups, and a Black Music and Rebellion event. The season celebrates Black British culture and history across the borough.

stories.headline: Black Patients in England Face Longer Delays at Every Stage of Breast Cancer Care
stories.summary: A University of Surrey study of 86,564 patients found Black patients in England had 29 percent lower odds of being diagnosed through screening and 37 percent higher odds of emergency diagnosis, with about five days longer to treatment.

stories.headline: Haitian Bridge Alliance Renews Call to Halt Deportations and Restore TPS for Haitians
stories.summary: The California-based Haitian Bridge Alliance called on the US administration to stop deportations to Haiti and on the Senate to restore Temporary Protected Status for more than 300,000 Haitians. The group cited gang violence and mass displacement in Haiti, alongside the State Department's Level 4 do-not-travel warning for the country.

stories.headline: Bethune-Cookman Stuns No. 1 Jackson State in the Final Minute as HBCU Football Delivers a Week of Upsets
stories.summary: Week 8 of the HBCU football season shook up both major conferences: Bethune-Cookman beat top-ranked Jackson State 24-21 on a touchdown pass with 40 seconds left, Howard won at Morgan State on an 87-yard interception return in overtime, and Texas Southern walked off Southern with a 46-yard field goal at its 99th homecoming.
